endorsements.quote: Versioning and change control should be applied to model inputs, thresholds, alert routing, and workflow rules because configuration shifts can redistribute delays and resources in practice ( 14 ).

Equity drift should be treated as a patient-safety risk: a baseline should be established before go-live, continuous monitoring should be conducted after launch, and the tool should be downgraded, rolled back, or disabled if harms or widening gaps emerge ( 6 ).

Minimum governance includes role-based access; immutable logs for model outputs, overrides, and pathway activations; and auditable system interfaces aligned with responsible-AI guidance and risk-management expectations.

Fairness should therefore be assessed at the service layer after deployment by auditing the chain of care—Trigger → Response → Resource-ready/arrival → Disposition → Outcomes—so that disparities can be localized to a specific link and paired with actionable workflow, communication, or capacity levers rather than inferred from model performance alone ( 6 , 14 ).

Equity drift should be treated as a patient-safety risk: a baseline should be established before go-live, continuous monitoring should be conducted after launch, and the tool should be downgraded, rolled back, or disabled if harms or widening gaps emerge ( 6 ).
AI can amplify these seams unless governance explicitly treats them as deployment targets ( 16 ).

Patients and families should receive a plain-language written explanation that the system is designed to support timely response—not to deny care—with a correction/appeal pathway when data are missing or an escalation decision is disputed ( 6 , 16 ).
MFAS affects equity only when each metric is explicitly bound to a controllable lever and a named owner ( 6 , 7 ).

MFAS governance requires cross-department ownership—obstetrics, anesthesia, ICU, blood bank, quality/safety, and health information technology (with data science support as needed)—to prevent an accountability vacuum in which a vendor “owns” the algorithm while clinicians own the consequences ( 6 ).
Any change to trigger logic, thresholds, routing, interfaces, or data-field mappings requires versioned change control and re-audit of chain metrics and stratified gaps.

A minimal cadence is sufficient: a monthly MFAS dashboard huddle reviews stratified run charts by chain link and assigns owners for clusters of over-window intervals; a quarterly cross-service review reassesses target windows, routing rules, and capacity plans; and sentinel events trigger rapid reconstruction of timestamps and immediate containment actions ( 14 ).

Operationalization should adopt risk-management language—treating equity as an accountable, measured, managed risk item—consistent with the National Institute of Standards and Technology AI Risk Management Framework ( 25 ).

Research should test whether MFAS chain metrics (trigger → response → resource-ready/arrival → disposition/outcome) mediate changes in maternal outcomes using pragmatic designs, including quasi-experiments, stepped-wedge rollouts, and quality improvement evaluations with interrupted time series.

unlisted_practices: Audit deployed AI-supported obstetric emergency care using a minimum fairness audit set of chain-of-care timestamps (trigger, response, resource-ready, disposition, outcome) with stratified delay distributions.
Define avoidable delay as a shared equity denominator with prespecified target windows, and report side-by-side aspirational clinical and current capability targets with ratcheted improvement plans.
Bind every audit metric gap to a controllable lever, named owner, deadline, and verification metric in a corrective-action register.
Assign one primary exception code to each over-window interval to attribute delays.
Pair equity corrective actions with balancing measures (alert burden, workforce load, capacity spillover, other-pathway delays) and throttle or roll back actions if thresholds worsen.
Provide patients and families a correction and appeal pathway for disputed escalation decisions or missing data.
Display disparity gaps as absolute differences, relative ratios, and pre/post trends rather than p-values.
Stratify equity audits by workflow-facing access proxies and, where lawful and governed, by protected attributes with privacy safeguards.
